hook: Andreessen co-created the Mosaic browser and co-founded Netscape in 1994 before co-founding the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz in 2009 with Ben Horowitz. The firm has since backed a wide range of AI companies, and Andreessen sits on the board of Meta Platforms.
name: Marc Andreessen

quote.context: Marc Andreessen, Why Software Is Eating the World, The Wall Street Journal, August 20, 2011

moniker: Co-founder and General Partner, Andreessen Horowitz

reading.body:
Marc Andreessen has deployed venture capital at scale to fund AI companies since 2009, positioning him as a primary allocator of private capital into the infrastructure and models powering AI development.

His path from creating the Mosaic browser and co-founding Netscape in the 1990s established his view that software transforms entire industries. That thesis informed his 2011 essay "Why Software Is Eating the World," which framed how software methodically expands into sectors previously built on hardware or human labor. Andreessen Horowitz, co-founded in 2009, became the vehicle to fund that expansion. Since its founding, the firm has backed a wide range of AI companies, making it one of the primary sources of capital flowing into AI startups and scaling efforts.

His board seat at Meta since 2008 connects his investor role to one of the largest consumers of compute infrastructure. Meta's vast data centers and power demands reflect the capital-intensive nature of building and running AI systems at scale. His dual position as investor and board member places him inside both the funding decisions that enable AI scaling and the operational constraints—buildings, power, compute—that limit it.

This data shows his influence on where capital flows into AI. It does not show how much capital Andreessen Horowitz has deployed into AI companies, how that compares to other venture firms, or whether his investment thesis has shifted since 2011 to account for the physical constraints now binding AI expansion.
